episodes.171993: Scattered to widespread thunderstorms developed over the Nebraska Sandhills during the early afternoon hours of August 31st. This activity gradually spread southeast into northwest portions of the NWS Hastings coverage area between 4-5 PM CDT, where air temperatures were in the 90s and instability was strong. However, deep layer wind shear was weak, which kept much of this activity from becoming severe and led to a gradual weakening trend as activity moved southeast during the evening hours. The only severe report from this event was a 58 MPH wind gust at the Lexington Airport in Dawson County. This gust actually occurred on the backside of the departing line of thunderstorms, suggesting it was associated with dry air interacting with the edge of departing stratiform rain. No damage reports were received from this area. Thunderstorms with this event were largely diurnally-driven given lack of wind shear, so activity quickly dissipated with loss of daytime heating around sunset.
episodes.172041: A severe thunderstorm that moved over Orlando Executive Airport produced a 62 mph wind gusts that flipped over two small planes, resulting in one fatality and one injury.
episodes.172659: An upper low-pressure system was over Northern Mexico. This feature resulted in increased upper lift and moisture across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These conditions produced heavy rain that lead to flash flooding across the area.
episodes.172743: A mid-level trough extended northeastward from northern Mexico through the Permian Basin. Enhanced atmospheric lift and rich low and mid-level moisture were across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These conditions contributed to heavy rain. This rain moved over saturated soils and resulted in flash flooding across parts of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico.
episodes.172744: A mid-level trough extended northeastward from northern Mexico through the Permian Basin. Enhanced atmospheric lift and rich low and mid-level moisture were across West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. These conditions contributed to heavy rain. This rain moved over saturated soils and resulted in flash flooding across parts of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico.
episodes.173030: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around west central Florida.
episodes.173166: A frontal boundary lingered over central GA and weakened while a mid level low deepened across southeast GA and lifted northeastward. A broad surface low was over the Suwannee Valley. Weak steering flow allowed both sea breezes to push inland in the afternoon and combined with high moisture with PWATs around 2-2.2 inches resulted in |scattered to numerous showers and storms. Stronger storms developed supported by mid level vorticity associated with the deepening low and lingering convergence along|the remnants of the frontal boundary.
episodes.173610: A lake enhanced band of thunderstorms developed along a front as it crossed to the east of Lake Ontario during the evening.
episodes.173616: During the afternoon a strong cold front moved south through Northwest Kansas.  Thunderstorms developed along the cold front as it moved through.  The wind gusts from some of these thunderstorms were as high as 69 MPH, with the highest wind gust report coming from Hill City.  As the front moved through there were also reductions in visibility to as low as a quarter mile from blowing dust.
episodes.173847: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. There were a few reports of trees and wires down, as well as isolated flooding.
episodes.173849: A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms moved into eastern Coffee county with flash flooding reported on Rucker Blvd near the Coffee-Dale County line.
episodes.174074: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon of the 1st across northern Oklahoma, with isolated flash flooding reported. Later additional thunderstorms developed in western Oklahoma with reports of severe wind gusts.
episodes.174149: A weak stationary front extended from Eastern Oklahoma across Northeast Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon hours of September 1st. Meanwhile, a shortwave trough shifted east across Oklahoma and North Texas, atop the stalled front during the afternoon and evening. This trough enhanced large scale forcing along the front, with pockets of differential heating resulting in needed instability to enhance shower and thunderstorm development. A band of near stationary thunderstorms developed over the city of Center in Central Shelby County, resulting in flash flooding where several vehicles stalled in high water.
episodes.174281: Afternoon thunderstorms developed over interior South Florida from a convergence of sea breezes from the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.
episodes.174340: River flooding from snowmelt and rainfall earlier this spring continued into and then ended in September due to dry conditions. The James River at the Columbia river gauge, CMBS2, was in minor flood stage (between 13 and 16 feet) for about 2 hours on the early morning of September 1st prior to falling below flood stage thereafter. It had been in flood stage since April 28th. Additionally, minor flooding (between 14 and 17 feet) persisted from September 1st through the early morning of September 23rd at the Stratford river gauge, SFDS2. It had been in flood stage since May 7th. Impacts were predominantly to agricultural lands.
episodes.174432: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along a stationary front that stretched west to east across southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms began developing around midday and produced frequent lightning strikes. One person was struck by lightning and several structures were impacted.
episodes.174433: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along a stationary front that stretched west to east across southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms began developing around midday and eventually drifted southward into southeast Georgia, producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.174435: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along a stationary front that stretched west to east across southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms eventually pushed southward and off the coast. One storm produced a brief waterspout just offshore of Folly Beach.
episodes.174463: A couple of isolated storms produced a couple of reports of damaging winds on September 1st, 2022.  One occurred in southeast Kansas and the other occurred in central Kansas.

The ASOS at Orlando Executive Airport, KORL, measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph from a severe thunderstorm. These winds flipped over two small planes at the airport. One plane was unoccupied when it was flipped near a hanger on the airport. A second plane that had two people onboard was flipped as it was taxiing on the  main runway. When first responders arrived they found one man had died from his injuries at the scene, and the other man was transported to Orlando Medical Regional Center with serious injuries.
